nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Hidetoshi Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2003): neutral atoms trapped in an optical lattice at a 'magic wavelength', where the light shifts of both clock states cancel, so that thousands of atoms can be interrogated simultaneously without perturbation. This combined the Lamb-Dicke confinement of ion clocks with the large atom numbers of neutral atoms. Katori's group realized the first lattice clocks with strontium and later cryogenic clocks; Jun Ye's group at JILA drove the concept to record accuracy and stability, reaching the 10^-18 to 10^-19 level and resolving gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. Lattice clocks now exceed caesium standards by two orders of magnitude, motivate the redefinition of the SI second, enable relativistic geodesy, and provide tabletop searches for dark matter and variations of fundamental constants. It is a truly platform-creating invention, used today by laboratories worldwide, including with ytterbium.
